title: Neural Audio Codecs — EnCodec, SNAC, Mimi, DAC and the Semantic-Acoustic Split

questions.question: With n_codebooks=4, what does rvq_encode return as its first result?
options: Four lists of codebook indices, one list per residual stage
One floating-point centroid for the whole signal
A single list containing four waveform samples
Four reconstructed waveforms with different sample rates
questions.explanation: rvq_encode appends one index list after each quantize_with_codebook call, so four stages produce four lists.

questions.question: A codebook has 8 centroids. How many bits does one selected centroid represent in main.py's bitrate calculation?
options: 8 bits
3 bits
4 bits
1 bit
questions.explanation: Eight choices require log2(8)=3 bits; the demo computes bits_per_frame as n_codebooks * 3.

questions.question: What is passed to the next RVQ stage after quantize_with_codebook processes a value v?
options: The integer index without any numeric residual
The original v again, so every stage sees the same signal
The residual v minus the selected centroid
The average of all centroids in the codebook
questions.explanation: The function stores v - codebook[idx] in residuals, and rvq_encode quantizes those residuals at the next stage.

questions.question: Why does rvq_decode add the selected centroids from all codebooks?
options: To remove the contribution of the first codebook
To make every decoded sample equal to the largest codebook index
To convert the indices into a probability distribution
To combine the coarse approximation and successive residual corrections
questions.explanation: Each later codebook models what the preceding stages missed, so summing their centroids reconstructs the signal estimate.

questions.question: For 4 codebooks of size 8 at 50 frames per second, what bitrate does the demo calculate?
options: 600 bps
400 bps
150 bps
questions.explanation: Each stage contributes 3 bits, giving 4*3=12 bits per frame; 12*50 is 600 bps.

questions.question: In the Mimi split described by the demo, which sequence matches the intended generation order?
options: Generate acoustic residuals first, then infer the semantic token from them
Generate codebook 0 for content, then codebooks 1–7 for acoustic detail
Generate all eight codebooks independently with no conditioning
Generate only codebook 7 because it contains the waveform
questions.explanation: The demo assigns WavLM-distilled content to codebook 0 and conditions the acoustic codebooks 1–7 on that semantic stream and speaker context.
